alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of an old printed title page inside an oval frame of beads, with bits of carved ornament, drapery and fruit in the corners. It reads "Pammelia. Musicks Miscellanie. Or, Mixed Varietie of Pleasant Roundelayes, and delightfull Catches, of 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. 9. 10. Parts in one.", then two lines in italics, a rule, and "London Printed by William Barley, for R. B. and H. W. and are to be sold at the Spread Eagle at the great North doore of Paules. 1609. Cum Priuilegio."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de una antigua portada impresa dentro de un marco ovalado de cuentas, con trozos de adorno tallado, cortinajes y frutas en las esquinas. Dice "Pammelia. Musicks Miscellanie. Or, Mixed Varietie of Pleasant Roundelayes, and delightfull Catches, of 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. 9. 10. Parts in one."; siguen dos líneas en cursiva, una raya y "London Printed by William Barley, for R. B. and H. W. and are to be sold at the Spread Eagle at the great North doore of Paules. 1609. Cum Priuilegio."

caption.en: The title page of Pammelia, printed in London by William Barley in 1609, the book of rounds and catches that holds the earliest known printing of this round, as No. 85.
caption.es: La portada de Pammelia, libro de cánones y catches impreso en Londres por William Barley en 1609, que contiene la primera impresión conocida de este canon, el n.º 85.

source: [Thomas Ravenscroft, compiler], Pammelia. Musicks Miscellanie (London: William Barley, 1609; STC 20759), title page (image n0); cropped to the printed title inside the oval

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of two staves of early printed music with diamond-shaped notes, numbered 85 and beginning with a large plain capital H. The words under them read "Ey ho no body at home, meate nor drinke, nor money haue I none, fill the pot Eadie. Hey, vt supra." Faint print from the other side of the leaf shows through, a small handwritten cross is beside the number, and part of a large printed letter stands at the bottom right.
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de dos pentagramas de música impresa antigua con notas en forma de rombo, con el número 85 y una gran H mayúscula sin adornos al principio. La letra debajo dice "Ey ho no body at home, meate nor drinke, nor money haue I none, fill the pot Eadie. Hey, vt supra." Se transparenta tenuemente la impresión del otro lado de la hoja, hay una pequeña cruz manuscrita junto al número y, abajo a la derecha, parte de una gran letra impresa.

caption.en: No. 85 as reprinted in the second edition of Pammelia (London, 1618): the large H begins the words, "Hey ho no body at home", and "Hey, vt supra" at the end sends each singer back to the start.
caption.es: El n.º 85 tal como se reimprimió en la segunda edición de Pammelia (Londres, 1618): la gran H inicia la letra, "Hey ho no body at home", y "Hey, vt supra" al final hace volver a cada cantante al principio.

source: [Thomas Ravenscroft, compiler], Pammelia. Musickes Miscellanie (London: Thomas Snodham for Mathew Lownes and John Browne, 1618; STC 20760), No. 85, sig. E3 (image n36); cropped to No. 85

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of old printed type headed in italics "The Knight of the burning Pestle." A speech marked "Oldmer." reads "Hang bread and supper, let's preserue our mirth, and we shall neuer feele hunger, I'le warrant you, let's haue a Catch, boy follow me, come sing this Catch." Then, in italics, "Ho, ho, no body at home, meate, nor drinke, nor money ha wee none, fill the pot Eedy, neuer more need I." Then "Oldmer. So boies enough, follow mee, let's change our place and we shall laugh afresh. Exeunt."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de texto impreso antiguo con el encabezado en cursiva "The Knight of the burning Pestle." Un parlamento marcado "Oldmer." dice "Hang bread and supper, let's preserue our mirth, and we shall neuer feele hunger, I'le warrant you, let's haue a Catch, boy follow me, come sing this Catch." Sigue, en cursiva, "Ho, ho, no body at home, meate, nor drinke, nor money ha wee none, fill the pot Eedy, neuer more need I." Y luego "Oldmer. So boies enough, follow mee, let's change our place and we shall laugh afresh. Exeunt."

caption.en: The Knight of the Burning Pestle, printed in London in 1613: the penniless Old Merrythought answers "Hang bread and supper" and calls for this catch, "Ho, ho, no body at home".
caption.es: The Knight of the Burning Pestle, impresa en Londres en 1613: el arruinado Old Merrythought responde "Hang bread and supper" y pide este catch, "Ho, ho, no body at home".

source: The Knight of the Burning Pestle (London: printed for Walter Burre, 1613; STC 1674), Act IV, sig. I2 (image n62); British Museum copy; cropped to the top of the page
